chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

No one prays the obligatory prayer upon a riding animal except a sick person; he is to be turned toward the qiblah, and Sūrat al-Fātiḥah suffices him, and in the obligatory prayer he places his face upon whatever he is able of something, and in the supererogatory prayer he gestures with a gesture.

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: gesturing as a substitute for fuller bodily movements
key_terms.الدَّابَّةِ: a riding animal or mount on which one is being carried
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer toward which one must be turned
key_terms.فَاتِحَةُ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, which suffices in this circumstance
key_terms.مَرِيضٌ: a sick person whose condition creates legal concession

ai.seo_question: Can a sick traveler perform the obligatory prayer on a riding animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the prayer of a sick traveler who prays in a litter or upon a riding animal. It distinguishes between the obligatory prayer and the supererogatory prayer, requiring orientation toward the qiblah and whatever degree of physical performance is possible in the obligatory prayer, while allowing gesturing in the supererogatory prayer.
